newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks start with bang, end with whimper.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks start with bang, end with whimper.

text.p: Swiss shares ran out of steam on Monday, giving up most of their early gains and slipping below Friday's close towards the end of the session.

"It was a little disappointing today", one dealer said, noting that some investors had hoped for a better performance given the U.S. dollar's strong rally above 1.40 Swiss francs and Friday's record Wall Street close.
"But we are at a very high level and the air is getting thin," he said, adding a fall below 4,000 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) seemed likely this week.
The SMI slid 10.3 points, or 0.26 percent, to 4,009.6, while the all-share SPI fell 4.40 points to 2,574.76.
Major pharmaceuticals Roche and Novartis were in the limelight. Novartis suffered from selling by British investors while Roche continued its bull run, dealers said.
Roche powered ahead 120 francs, or 1.09 percent, to 11,170 francs after hitting a record high at 11,195 earlier in the day.
Novartis was pressured by some selling in reaction to steep gains shares of Ciba and Sandoz had posted ahead of the two companies' merger as Novartis in December, dealers said.
Trade on the Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) was very quiet, with Credit Suisse, UBS and Roche standing out, dealers said.
